positions.summary_short: Austin is running on a promise of urgent city revival centred on safety, affordability and prosperity.
summary_bullets: Describes her candidacy as 'an extreme intervention to execute the revival of our city.'
Says she would expedite safety, affordability and prosperity for citizens citywide.
Presents herself as the only candidate with a lifetime of frontline service in healthcare, outreach, public administration, social services, governance and fiscal watchdog work.
positions.verbatim_quote: I am running for Hamilton Mayor as an extreme intervention to execute the revival of our city. To expedite safety, affordability & prosperity to our city wide citizens.
positions.source_title: Municipal Election Candidate Profiles - North End Breezes (candidate-submitted profile)

positions.summary_short: Cooper would cap tax increases at the rate of inflation, arguing past tax hikes delivered worse services.
summary_bullets: His plan is to cap property tax increases at the rate of inflation: never higher, sometimes lower.
Cites a 23% tax increase over the last four years alongside worse roads, violent crime and homelessness, arguing 'throwing money against problems' made life worse.
Criticizes city budgeting as having 'no actuals, no benchmarks, no peer data' and service levels from 2014, calling the budget 'a guess.'
Says he decided to run for mayor after being ruled out of order for trying to cap taxes as a councillor, being told only the mayor can set the tax rate under strong mayor powers.
positions.verbatim_quote: My plan is to cap taxes at rate of inflation, which means we're not going to exceed inflation.
positions.source_title: FULL TRANSCRIPT: Hamilton Mayoral Candidate Rob Cooper Answers 20 Detailed Questions on The 155 Podcast - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Cooper set a goal of zero homelessness within four years.
summary_bullets: Frames homelessness as mental health, drug addiction, trauma and violent crime.
Sets a goal of zero homelessness in four years, with details on his campaign website.
positions.verbatim_quote: And going back to homelessness, my goal in four years is zero homeless.
positions.source_title: FULL TRANSCRIPT: Hamilton Mayoral Candidate Rob Cooper Answers 20 Detailed Questions on The 155 Podcast - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Cooper names violent crime a top priority and wants Hamilton to be the safest city in Ontario.
summary_bullets: Names violent crime as a top priority alongside taxes, citing indiscriminate gun violence including stray bullets killing bystanders.
Says Hamilton is 'unsafe and dangerous' and argues the problem must be defined before it can be fixed.
Wants Hamilton to be the safest place in Ontario.
positions.verbatim_quote: making our city the safest place in Ontario
positions.source_title: FULL TRANSCRIPT: Hamilton Mayoral Candidate Rob Cooper Answers 20 Detailed Questions on The 155 Podcast - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Cooper prefers collaborative governance but would use strong mayor powers on taxes, and would hire a transformational city manager plus a Chief HR Officer.
summary_bullets: Prefers a collaborative model with councillors, with a mayor's-office staffer responsible for the mayor-council relationship.
Would use strong mayor powers on the tax rate if council pushed increases he opposed.
Would hire a 'transformational' city manager and, as a key hire, a Chief Human Resources Officer to fix culture, succession and compensation issues.
Wants neutral, trained chairs for council committees instead of the current rotating-chair model he calls dysfunctional.
positions.verbatim_quote: My preference is to work with the councillors.
positions.source_title: FULL TRANSCRIPT: Hamilton Mayoral Candidate Rob Cooper Answers 20 Detailed Questions on The 155 Podcast - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Gillespie centres her platform on affordable housing, tenant protections and community-led safety.
summary_bullets: As mayor would prioritize community-led safety initiatives, affordable housing, and a thriving arts sector.
Has fought for tenant protections and infrastructure maintenance at CityHousing Hamilton.
Platform priorities include housing, tenant protections, climate justice, transparency at city hall, community-led initiatives and strengthening the arts sector.
positions.verbatim_quote: As your Mayor, she will prioritize community-led safety initiatives, affordable housing, and a thriving arts sector.
positions.source_title: Scarlett for Mayor - A Mayor for the People

positions.summary_short: Gillespie advocates for climate justice and transparency in local government.
summary_bullets: Advocates for climate justice as part of her platform.
Links climate advocacy with transparency in local government.
positions.verbatim_quote: advocating for climate justice and transparency in local government
positions.source_title: Scarlett for Mayor - A Mayor for the People

positions.summary_short: Gillespie would treat arts as civic infrastructure, review the City Enrichment Fund for inflation, and protect affordable cultural space.
summary_bullets: Calls arts and culture 'essential civic infrastructure,' part of economic development, downtown revitalization, neighbourhood planning and community wellbeing - not an optional expense.

Would request a comprehensive early-term review of the City Enrichment Fund with artists and sector representatives, supporting inflationary adjustments and sustainable supplementary revenues (including Municipal Accommodation Tax revenues).

Would create a citywide inventory of at-risk cultural spaces including underused city-owned properties, review municipal venue rental rates, and explore long-term affordable leases and shared cultural hubs.

Would establish a regular ongoing arts-and-culture roundtable with HACC, independent artists and grassroots organizations, with early consultation before major decisions and public reporting of what was heard.
positions.verbatim_quote: I would treat arts and culture as part of economic development, downtown revitalization, neighbourhood planning and community wellbeing, and not as an optional expense considered only after other priorities.
positions.source_title: CANDIDATE SURVEY: HAMILTON MUNICIPAL ELECTION 2026 - Hamilton City Magazine (Hamilton Arts Council survey)

positions.summary_short: Horwath is running on a seven-point tariff response plan and downtown revitalization, citing the $300M TD Coliseum deal.
summary_bullets: Named fighting Trump tariffs a top platform priority: she put out a seven-point plan and circulated a motion to council (passed unanimously) to protect Hamilton businesses, workers and community.
Named downtown revitalization another top plank, calling downtown 'the front door' and 'heartbeat' of the city.
Cited getting the TD Coliseum deal over the finish line, growing its investment from $50M to $300M.
positions.verbatim_quote: One of the platform priorities I have is fighting against the Trump tariffs.
positions.source_title: FULL TRANSCRIPT: Hamilton Mayoral Candidate Andrea Horwath Answers 20 Detailed Questions on The 155 Podcast - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Horwath proposed a 4.25% 2026 tax increase, framed as holding the line on affordability while funding roads, infrastructure and transit.
summary_bullets: Set a proposed 2026 tax budget increase of 4.25%, framed as 'holding the line on affordability.'
Says the budget focuses on fixing roads, renewing aging infrastructure, investing in transit and supporting community safety.
Says the city must work smarter, find efficiencies and ensure tax dollars are used wisely.
positions.verbatim_quote: holding the line on affordability by setting a proposed increase of 4.25%
positions.source_title: Statement from Mayor Regarding the 2026 Proposed Tax Budget | City of Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Horwath says she is building more housing, attracting investment and securing senior-government support.
summary_bullets: Says 'We are building Hamilton: building more housing, attracting investment and finally securing the support from other levels of government our city deserves.'
Is running for re-election to 'build on that momentum,' citing knowledge of the job and a record of results.
positions.verbatim_quote: We are building Hamilton: building more housing, attracting investment and finally securing the support from other levels of government our city deserves.
positions.source_title: Municipal Election Candidate Profiles - North End Breezes (candidate-submitted profile)

positions.summary_short: Loomis would coordinate infrastructure work via 'Dig Once Hamilton,' add a rural infrastructure strategy, and better connect HSR, LRT and GO.
summary_bullets: 'Getting Hamilton Moving Again': every Hamiltonian should get where they need to go safely, reliably and efficiently.
Would introduce 'Dig Once Hamilton,' a city-wide approach to coordinate infrastructure work, reduce disruption and get better value from road investments.
Would introduce a Rural Hamilton Infrastructure Strategy for rural roads, bridges, culverts and drainage, prioritized by safety, condition and community needs.
Would launch 'Routes to Opportunity' to improve connections between HSR, LRT and GO and address transportation gaps for residents facing barriers.
positions.verbatim_quote: As mayor, Keanin Loomis will introduce Dig Once Hamilton, a city-wide approach to coordinate infrastructure work, reduce disruption and ensure Hamilton gets better value from every road and infrastructure investment.
positions.source_title: Keanin Loomis for Mayor - Mobility (SMART Plan)

positions.summary_short: Loomis makes safety his number-one SMART Plan plank, with a coordinated downtown response to homelessness, mental health and public disorder.
summary_bullets: His SMART Plan stands for Safety, Mobility, Accountability, Responsive Government and Taxpayer Respect.
Safety is the number-one plank: says residents across the community lack confidence in Hamilton's future because of what is playing out on downtown streets.

First-100-day agenda: hire the next city manager, pass the first budget, and make an appreciable impact downtown - particularly on homelessness - via a far more coordinated response to homelessness, mental health and public disorder.
positions.verbatim_quote: There's a reason why safety is number one.
positions.source_title: FULL TRANSCRIPT: Hamilton Mayoral Candidate Keanin Loomis Answers 20 Detailed Questions on The 155 Election Podcast - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Loomis's 100-day agenda starts with hiring the city manager and passing a budget.
summary_bullets: Top items of his first 100-day agenda: hire the next city manager (calls it the most important and first decision), get the first budget passed, and make an appreciable downtown impact on homelessness.
Says he cannot yet say what the tax rate will be because he would 'inherit your mess' from the current administration.
positions.verbatim_quote: First, hire the next city manager, because that's the most important decision I will make and the very first decision I need to make.
positions.source_title: FULL TRANSCRIPT: Hamilton Mayoral Candidate Keanin Loomis Answers 20 Detailed Questions on The 155 Election Podcast - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Loomis would grow the City Enrichment Fund with demand, pilot 'meanwhile leases' for vacant spaces, and keep an open door to the arts sector.
summary_bullets: Calls arts and culture 'one of Hamilton's biggest competitive advantages' and an integral part of his economic development strategy.
Would commit to reviewing and strengthening the City Enrichment Fund in collaboration with the sector, growing it alongside demand once finances are back on track.
Would explore a 'meanwhile lease' approach letting artists temporarily use vacant spaces, and cut City Hall fees, red tape and permit delays for cultural venues.
As mayor would keep a direct line to artists and organizations, work with HACC as the city-wide convening body, and bring the sector in early on funding, cultural space and downtown planning.
positions.verbatim_quote: I see arts and culture as an integral part of Hamilton's economic development strategy.
positions.source_title: CANDIDATE SURVEY: HAMILTON MUNICIPAL ELECTION 2026 - Hamilton City Magazine (Hamilton Arts Council survey)

positions.summary_short: Loomis pledged to oppose AI data centres lacking stringent, enforceable regulations.
summary_bullets: At the televised debate, when challenged by Gillespie on AI data centres, Loomis answered 'yes, absolutely' to opposing any data centre without appropriately stringent and enforceable regulations.
positions.verbatim_quote: yes, absolutely
positions.source_title: Summary and Replay: Hamilton's Televised Mayoral Debate 2026 - TPR Hamilton

positions.summary_short: Yan would grow the City Enrichment Fund, protect affordable cultural space in downtown planning, and partner with the arts sector continuously.
summary_bullets: Calls arts and culture essential economic and social infrastructure, citing $1.29B in GDP and 15,000+ jobs.

Would commit to reviewing and strengthening the City Enrichment Fund via a transparent review of funding levels, application processes and unmet demand, growing it as the fiscal position permits and seeking private-sector and senior-government partnerships.
Would protect and create affordable studio, rehearsal, performance and exhibition space as part of downtown planning, with city-owned space kept accessible and cost-recovery or below-market rates.
Would establish regular dialogue with artists, arts organizations and HACC, with early involvement in policies and transparent follow-up on recommendations.
positions.verbatim_quote: As Mayor, I would treat arts and culture as an investment in Hamilton's future—not merely another expense in the municipal budget.
positions.source_title: CANDIDATE SURVEY: HAMILTON MUNICIPAL ELECTION 2026 - Hamilton City Magazine (Hamilton Arts Council survey)
